expo.name: GoalSlot
expo.description: GoalSlot turns your goals into a schedule you actually follow — plan your day, track tasks, and time your focus sessions, online or off.

ios._infoPlistComment: Both usage strings below are ALSO written by the expo-speech-recognition config plugin, which supplies generic defaults. They are declared here explicitly because these two are App Store review copy, not plumbing: a missing NSMicrophoneUsageDescription is an outright rejection and a silent crash the first time the mic is touched, and a vague one ('Allow GoalSlot to use the microphone') gets flagged for not saying what the data is used for. Keeping them in app.json means they are reviewable in a diff instead of buried in a node_modules plugin's fallback. The plugin honours an existing value rather than overwriting it. This key sits outside infoPlist on purpose — anything inside that object is written verbatim into Info.plist.

infoPlist.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: GoalSlot uses the microphone so you can speak commands like "start tracking my deen goal" instead of typing them. Audio is only captured while you are holding the mic button.
infoPlist.NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription: GoalSlot turns what you say into text so it can start timers, add tasks, and move schedule blocks for you. Recognition runs on your device where the device supports it.

android._permissionsComment: EXACT ALARMS — what makes a schedule reminder land ON the minute. expo-notifications picks its AlarmManager method at runtime: `if (SDK_INT < S || canScheduleExactAlarms()) setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(...) else setAndAllowWhileIdle(...)`. Without these, that check fails on Android 12+ and every reminder degrades to the INEXACT branch, which Doze can defer by many minutes — a 9:00 block announcing itself at 9:20. SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM covers API 31-32; USE_EXACT_ALARM covers API 33+ and is required on Android 14+, where the former is no longer auto-granted. PLAY POLICY: USE_EXACT_ALARM is restricted to apps whose core function is an alarm clock or calendar — confirm before the next Play submission. Dropping it still leaves exact alarms working on Android 12-13. RECORD_AUDIO — voice control; also added by the expo-speech-recognition plugin, declared here so the app's full permission set is readable from app.json alone. That plugin additionally writes the Android 11+ <queries> entry for the android.speech.RecognitionService intent, which cannot be expressed here and without which SpeechRecognizer reports itself unavailable on every device running Android 11 or later.

plugins._comment: NON-FUNCTIONAL PLACEHOLDER. No `organization`/`project` set — no real Sentry project exists yet (out of scope for this change, same rule as `eas init`/EAS Updates below). Without them the plugin falls back to SENTRY_ORG/SENTRY_PROJECT env vars at native-build time, which also aren't set, so this stays inert. It only affects native source-map upload config, not JS runtime behavior — see src/lib/sentry.ts for the runtime guard.

plugins.microphonePermission: GoalSlot uses the microphone so you can speak commands like "start tracking my deen goal" instead of typing them. Audio is only captured while you are holding the mic button.
plugins.speechRecognitionPermission: GoalSlot turns what you say into text so it can start timers, add tasks, and move schedule blocks for you. Recognition runs on your device where the device supports it.

widgets.name: TodayWidget
widgets.label: GoalSlot — Today
widgets.description: Your next scheduled block, or today's progress. Tap to open the app.

extra._messagingComment: Origin of the jiffy-messaging deployment. Null = messaging is off in this build: the Messages screens stay unregistered, the drawer entry is hidden, and no socket or token request is ever made. Override per environment with EXPO_PUBLIC_MESSAGING_URL / EXPO_PUBLIC_MESSAGING_WS_URL — app.config.js layers those on top of these, and derives the ws:// URL from the http:// one when only the latter is set.

updates._comment: NON-FUNCTIONAL PLACEHOLDER. `url` needs a real EAS project ID, which only exists after running `eas init`/`eas update:configure` against an Expo account — explicitly out of scope for this change. `enabled: false` keeps expo-updates from trying to check this placeholder URL at runtime (it would otherwise fail every launch). Flip `enabled` to true and swap in the real https://u.expo.dev/<project-id> URL once EAS is set up.
